transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been having a really hard time following through on instructions and actually finishing my tasks at work and at home. On top of that, I just feel constantly restless and find myself fidgeting all the time. It's making it really difficult to get anything done lately.
Have you struggled with these issues of attention and restlessness since your childhood (before age 12), or is this something that started more recently?

Yes, I've actually struggled with these issues since I was a kid, definitely well before I turned 12. I remember having a really hard time finishing my schoolwork and staying still back then too, though it has felt particularly bothersome lately.
When you feel restless, is it accompanied by constant, excessive worry about various everyday things, or is it more of a physical urge to keep moving?
It is definitely more of a physical urge to keep moving. I feel this constant need to fidget, tap my feet, or squirm in my seat, rather than feeling anxious or worried about everyday things.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates included all three ADHD presentations and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Based on the patient's clarification, the restlessness is a physical urge to move rather than a result of excessive worry, which rules out Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Furthermore, because the patient exhibits significant symptoms of both inattention (difficulty finishing tasks and following instructions) and hyperactivity/impulsivity (constant restlessness, fidgeting, and squirming) since childhood, the diagnosis can be narrowed down to Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation).
